source.title: Can Cross-Layer Transcoders Replace Vision Transformer Activations? An Interpretable Perspective on Vision
source.authors: Gerasimos Chatzoudis; Konstantinos D. Polyzos; Zhuo-Wei Li; Di-Fei Gu; Gemma E. Moran; Hao Wang; Dimitris N. Metaxas

record.file_problem: none noted; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper gives superposition as background and cites the original toy-model work, but its experiments evaluate CLTs as sparse reconstruction proxies for ViT MLP blocks. It does not test feature overlap, superposition geometry, or the listed LLM claims.
record.gate_note: The paper describes superposition and SAEs in related work, but reports no experiment on whether features overlap, whether networks drop features, polysemanticity, or feature dimensionality. Table 1 does report CLT reconstruction from sparse codes in vision models; these results are recorded as related findings, not as tests of the listed versions. Replacement accuracies and attribution ablations concern the CLT proxy, not the claim's feature geometry.
record.test_reason: The paper cites superposition (ref 12) only as background in related work. It uses sparse cross-layer transcoders as an interpretability tool on CLIP ViTs and reports that method's own performance: reconstruction R2/MSE/cosine, zero-shot accuracy under replacement, and attribution ablations. It reports no measurement of feature overlap, polysemanticity, feature dimensionality, or LLM feature recovery, so no version is tested. This fits T4 (relies on sparse dictionaries as a tool, reports only its method's performance) rather than T6, since it builds on the SAE/dictionary premise.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that CLTs are faithful, sparse, depth-aware proxies for ViT MLP blocks: they preserve zero-shot accuracy for [CLS] and late-layer replacement, and their attribution shows patch tokens are diagonal-dominant while [CLS] aggregates across depth. They draw no conclusion about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains cross-layer sparse encoders and decoders to reconstruct ViT post-MLP activations; it does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction varies across dataset, ViT backbone, and sparsity variant; the authors report ViT-B/16 is generally easier to approximate and ReLU-Top-k is strongest on ViT-B/32 in the reported aggregate comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: CLTs (expansion 16, k=128) reconstruct CLIP ViT post-MLP activations with layer-averaged R2 0.85–0.95 across three datasets and three sparsifiers. Fidelity dips in middle layers (R2 about 0.80–0.86 at layers 7–9 on ViT-B/32 CIFAR-100).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse cross-layer dictionaries reconstruct most variance of ViT MLP outputs, with fidelity lowest in middle layers.

record.problems: The reported reconstruction metrics are averages over layers and tokens; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The study does not measure feature overlap or feature geometry, and its sparse proxy is a CLT rather than an SAE.
record.rows_left_out: No further rows retained. Reconstruction cosine/MSE accompany the same Table 1 conditions and do not alter the sparse-reconstruction finding; replacement accuracy and attribution-ablation outcomes address CLT proxy fidelity and layer contributions rather than the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, no feature overlap, orthogonality, sparsity transition or geometry.
All: no analysis of neuron polysemanticity or of capacity allocation.
All: no analysis of the causes of polysemanticity.
All: the subjects are vision models, not LLMs. Sparse-code reconstruction is reported as method performance, not as evidence of feature spreading.
All: completeness, stability or canonicity of dictionary features is not assessed.
All: feature dimensionality is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation 'discusses' overstates the engagement: superposition appears only in one related-work sentence. The tranche is changed from T6 to T4 because the paper uses sparse dictionary methods as its tool. Because no version is tested, no labels are given. The 'observed' states on r1–r18 are not meaningful against claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry are not tested.
The capacity-based explanation of polysemanticity and dedicated-versus-shared dimensions are not tested.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition are not tested.
The experiments are on vision models, not LLMs, and use CLTs rather than testing whether an SAE recovers LLM features.
Completeness, stability, and canonical status of dictionary features are not evaluated.
The dimensionality and geometry of individual features are not evaluated.
